book.title: The Ashwood Chronicles
book.author: Example Author
book.description:
When 19-year-old Mira Valen finds a glowing spark in Ashwood she has no idea it will cost her her memory. Hunted by the governor and betrayed by her mentor, she must find the Ash Keeper - and decide what her memories are worth.

This file is a showcase: it demonstrates every feature of AuthorBoard with a fictional novel project.

notes.title: Mira Valen
notes.content:
Mira Valen
Raised as an orphan by a healer. She carries the fire of the Ash Keeper, without knowing what it costs. Seems tough and defiant but constantly doubts herself.
Inner journey: from fear of her own power to the decision to use it deliberately - and to pay the price.

notes.title: Kaelen Dorn
notes.content: A scar over his left eye. He rarely speaks but keeps every promise - except one. His true loyalty belongs to Lord Veyr, who holds his sister hostage.

attributes.name: Occupation
attributes.value: Knight of the Order of the Ashlight

notes.title: Lord Veyr
notes.content: Charismatic, polite, cruel. He wants to seal the Ash Spring - not out of malice but out of fear of what awakens with it.

notes.title: Tom the Ferryman
notes.content: Talks without pause but knows more than he admits. Years ago he ferried Kaelen's sister across the river.

notes.title: Isolde Wren
notes.content: Sharp, nervous, never without ink on her fingers. She is looking for the forbidden diary of the first Ash Keeper.

notes.title: The Ash Keeper
notes.content: Speaks with the voice of the forest. Remembers everyone who carried the fire before Mira - and everyone who broke under it.

notes.title: Ashwood
notes.content: Since the Great Fire black trunks reach into the sky, yet between the roots something still glows. In autumn everything smells of cold smoke.

notes.title: Hohenfels Castle
notes.content: Seat of the governor. Three curtain walls and a tower that never lies in shadow.

notes.title: Mistharbor
notes.content: Always fog, always gulls. The Mist Guild decides what goes in and out here - secrets included.

notes.title: The Archive of Karrow
notes.content: Vaults from the time before the Order. The parchment whispers when you come too close.

notes.title: The Ash Spring
notes.content: A pool of liquid embers in the heart of Ashwood. Whoever steps in gives something up - usually a memory.

notes.title: Order of the Ashlight
notes.content: Founded after the fall of the Observatory. Once keepers of knowledge, now the governor's tool.

notes.title: The Mist Guild
notes.content: Smugglers, traders, informants. Neutral as long as the pay is right.

notes.title: Spark Call
notes.content: The first spell Mira masters by instinct. Works best at dusk.

notes.title: Ash Oath
notes.content: Whoever breaks it burns from within. Isolde finds it in the diary of the first Ash Keeper.

notes.title: Chapter 1 - The First Spark
notes.content:
Autumn came early to Ashwood, and with it the smell of cold smoke that had hung in the trees since the Great Fire. Mira Valen was gathering mushrooms at the edge of the forest when the ground began to hum beneath her feet. It was not a tremor but a whisper that crept through her boots and settled in her chest. She dropped the basket. Between the charred roots a single spark glowed, hardly larger than a seed - and it looked at her.
She knew the stories: of the The Ash Keeper, who watched over the forests, of people he touched who were never the same again. Mira had always taken them for old wives' tales. Now she reached out, and the spark jumped onto her skin, warming her without burning.
"At last," said a voice that seemed to come from the forest itself. "It took so long."

comments.text: Great opening image - echo it in the epilogue.
Make clear here that only Mira can see it.

notes.title: Chapter 2 - Fog over the Harbor
notes.content:
Mistharbor welcomed Mira with the cry of gulls and the stench of tar and old fish. Tom the Ferryman had pulled her from the river that morning after the governor's men chased her to the landing, and he had not stopped talking since. „The girl with the fire" he muttered, rubbing his beard. "Lord Veyr pays good gold for such a thing, but Tom has never sold what fate put in his boat."
In a harbor tavern Mira met Isolde Wren, an archivist from Karrow searching for a book that should not exist. She spoke quietly and quickly, and when Mira laid the The Ash Staff on the table she grew quieter still. "Where did you get that?" - "From Ashwood." - "Then we have little time."

notes.title: Chapter 3 - The Archive
notes.content:
The Archive of Karrow lay deep beneath the city, in vaults older than the Order of the Ashlight. Isolde Wren led Mira through corridors where the parchment whispered when you passed too close. Dust lay on everything like a promise.
In a locked chest they found the diary of a woman who had called the Ash Keeper nine hundred years ago - and paid the price. Every page ended with the same sentence: Whoever carries the fire also carries forgetting. Mira read it three times until the letters blurred. Then she heard footsteps. Someone was following them through the shelves. (source: diary edition)

notes.title: Chapter 4 - Betrayal at Hohenfels
notes.content:
Hohenfels Castle perched above the valley like a bird of prey. Kaelen Dorn had promised Mira she would be safe there, and he had believed it when he said it. Only when the gates closed behind her and Lord Veyr came smiling down the stairs did she understand whose signet ring he wore on his finger.
"You should have known," Kaelen said quietly. "I never lied to you. I just did not tell you everything."
Mira felt the spark flare in her chest. For the first time she wanted it to burn.

notes.title: Scene 1.1 - Sparks in the Undergrowth
notes.content: The Great Fire as Mira remembers it as a child: smoke, screams, a hand pulling her from the flames. Cut back to the present.

notes.title: Scene 1.2 - The Speaking Forest
notes.content: The Ash Keeper speaks for the first time. Mira runs - and the forest will not let go of her.

notes.title: Scene 2.1 - Gulls and Shadows
notes.content: Arrival in Mistharbor. Tom shows her how to disappear in this town.

notes.title: Scene 3.1 - The Whispering Parchment
notes.content: Change of perspective: Isolde watches Mira begin to glow as she reads and knows she has just released something dangerous.

notes.title: Scene 4.1 - The Gate Closes
notes.content: Kaelen's view of the betrayal. He counts the steps to the cell and tries not to remember how she trusted him.

notes.title: Scene 5.1 - Embers in the Water
notes.content: Mira steps into the spring. Draft: the dialogue with the Ash Keeper still explains too much - trim later.

notes.title: Idea: Mirror world of ash
notes.content: Book 2: Beyond the spring lies a mirror of the world in which everything has burned. Whoever dies there is extinguished forever.

notes.title: Idea: Prologue from the Keeper's view
notes.content: A short prologue, only 300 words: the Keeper sees the first spark in a child and remembers.

notes.title: Research: Fire rituals in the Middle Ages
notes.content: Midsummer fires, cleansing fires, trials by ordeal. Interesting for the Ash Oath: oaths were sworn over flames. Open the source in the browser (Ctrl+click)

notes.title: Research: Shipping on the north coast
notes.content: Ferry times, draft of the boats, pilotage. Tom's ferry needs help from the guild at low tide.

notes.title: Style guide
notes.content: Close third person, past tense. No place names without a sensory impression. No explanatory dialogue longer than three lines. Use smoke, ash and embers sparingly - not every scene needs fire.

notes.title: Open questions
notes.content: Why does Veyr hold Kaelen's sister? When does Mira learn of the price? How much does the diary reveal? Must Isolde survive?
